question: Posterior capsular opacification (PCO) occurring months after successful cataract surgery represents a surgical complication that requires reoperation on the original cataract wound.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: FALSE. PCO (posterior capsule opacification) is a predictable biological event, not a surgical error. It is treated with Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy in the outpatient setting. This distinction is important when counselling patients preoperatively.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. PCO is NOT a surgical complication — it is a natural biological response: residual lens epithelial cells proliferate on the posterior capsule. Treatment is Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy, a clinic procedure (not a re-operation through the original wound).
